dedupe_keys.name: global exposure and risk database multi hazard exposure and risk of critical infrastructure admin 2

description: The Global Exposure and Risk Database gives global estimates of critical infrastructure exposure and risk from pluvial, fluvial and coastal flooding, earthquakes, tropical cyclones and rainfall- and earthquake-triggered landslides, summarised for every Admin-2 area of the GADM boundaries. S. Nirandjan and Elco Koks of the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam released version 1.0.0 in September 2026 with their multiple-hazard risk study. Seven exposure workbooks cover energy, transport, telecommunication, waste, water, education and healthcare assets, reporting exposed kilometres, square metres or counts per return period, and a risk workbook gives expected annual damages per sector and hazard as the median, minimum, quartiles and maximum across vulnerability curves and reconstruction costs. Coverage is global. Format and access: nine Excel files and a zip of design-standard sensitivity runs on Zenodo. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: results are aggregated to Admin-2, they depend on assumed design standards, and the asset inputs come from open global mapping. It supports global and national hazard exposure, resilience and adaptation investment screening. Related catalogue records are the Critical Infrastructure Spatial Index and the MIRACA pan-European exposure database.
